Leduc, Andrew, Yanxin Xu, Gergana Shipkovenska, Zhixun Dou, and Nikolai Slavov. 2025. “Limiting the Impact of Protein Leakage in Single-Cell Proteomics.” Nature Communications 16 (1): 4169.

leduc2025_pSCoPE.Rd

Single-cell proteomics data from primary mouse tracheal epithelial cells prepared fresh immediately after tissue dissociation. Each cell was stained with Sytox Green before sorting, so the dataset carries a per-cell measure of membrane permeabilisation alongside the protein quantifications. The dataset contains quantitative information on 928 fresh single cells. Only about 4% of these cells were permeabilised, which makes the dataset a baseline for comparison with cells affected by protein leakage.

Only the fresh cells are included. The frozen cells from the same study are not part of this dataset because no identification file was available for them.

Format

A QFeatures object with 34 sets, each being a SingleCellExperiment object:

  • Sets 1-32: PSM data with identifications and quantitive data - results from a MaxQuant database search.

  • Set 33 ("Peptides"): processed peptide data containing quantitative data coming from the PSM data. Taken from the source material.

  • Set 44 ("Proteins"): processed protein data containing quantitative data coming from the peptide data.

The colData(leduc2025_pSCoPE()) contains cell type and batch annotations that are common to all assays.

Source

The data were downloaded from the Slavov Lab website via a shared Goodle Drive folder. The raw data, identification and quantification data can also be found in the MassIVE repository MSV000094790: ftp://massive-ftp.ucsd.edu/v07/MSV000094790/.

The data used and generated as part of the scpdata repackaging is available in the Zenodo archive.

Acquisition protocol

The data were acquired using the following setup. More information can be found in the source article (see References).

  • Tissue dissociation: whole tracheas from 4-month-old male C57BL/6 mice were dissociated for 30 minutes at 37 °C with a papain, collagenase I, hyaluronidase, DNase and dispase enzyme cocktail.

  • Cell isolation: CellenOne sorting

  • Sample preparation: nPOP sample preparation. Cell lysis (DMSO and heat) was followed by overnight trypsin digestion, then TMTpro 35-plex labelling. Labelled samples were pooled and dried for injection. Channel 126C was used as a carrier and 127N as a reference. Cells were labeled in sets of 29.

  • Separation: online nLC (Vanquish Neo UHPLC) with a 25 cm x 75 µm IonOpticks column.

  • Mass spectrometry: Orbitrap Exploris 480 with prioritised data acquisition (pSCoPE).

  • Data analysis: MaxQuant 2.4.3.0 searched against the murine SwissProt database (downloaded 30 July 2018; 20,386 entries) at 1% FDR. Downstream analysis was performed in R using the QuantQC package.

Data collection

Raw and searched mass spectrometry data are available from the MassIVE repository (accession MSV000094790). Processed data are available from the Slavov lab website (see Source).

The necessary files for reproducing the QFeatures object are: - evidence.txt - celltype_annotation_fresh.csv - meta_fresh.csv - peptides.txt - proteinGroups.txt

All data come from the author distribution.

References

Leduc, Andrew, Yanxin Xu, Gergana Shipkovenska, Zhixun Dou, and Nikolai Slavov. 2025. “Limiting the Impact of Protein Leakage in Single-Cell Proteomics.” Nature Communications 16 (1): 4169. (link to article).
